Two grey rounded panels side by side, each with the same four children standing in a row on a grey oval shadow, labelled under their feet A, B, C, D (left to right), plus a teacher (woman in a sari, holding a clipboard) standing at the left end of the panel, facing the children. LEFT panel (before): teal speech bubble from the teacher: 'Let us play "Statue". Keep turning around ...'. A (boy, khaki shirt, brown shorts, hands raised in front), B (girl, khaki shirt, brown skirt), C (boy), D (girl, hair in a bunch) all stand side by side facing roughly towards the viewer/teacher side, bodies front-on or angled slightly. RIGHT panel (after): teal speech bubble from the teacher: 'STATUE!'. Same four children frozen in new facing directions compared with the left panel: A has his BACK to the viewer (facing away); B faces the viewer but turned slightly to the viewer's left (body angled), her hand touches C's arm; C faces the viewer/front (same way as before), one hand raised to his ear; D shows her side (profile) facing the viewer's right. The picture is used to compare each child's final facing direction with the starting one (A = back turned, B = part turn, C = same as start, D = side-on). Labels A, B, C, D appear under the children in both panels.

In a lavender rounded box (left part): two hands each holding one drinking straw; the straws are joined at their lower ends by a paper clip and open up in a V shape: the green-and-white striped straw goes up to the left, the yellow-and-white striped straw goes up to the right, each about 45 degrees from vertical, so they make an angle of about 90 degrees at the clip (bottom, centre). Beside it (middle): the two straws shown separately and nearly parallel: the green striped straw vertical, the yellow striped straw leaning slightly (top tilted a little right), and two paper clips lying below them (one brown, one grey). It models an angle made by turning one straw about a fixed one.

Header row (pink): 'Object' | 'Less than a 1/4 turn' | '1/4 turn' | 'More than a 1/4 turn' (the fraction is printed as a stacked 1 over 4 each time). First column (light green cells), top to bottom: Clothes clip, Door with hinge, Tongs, Scissors, File cover. Below the table are two bullet questions with dotted answer lines (names of objects that make a half turn / a full turn).

A giant (Ferris) wheel drawn front-on: a large circle (rim) with 24 coloured passenger cabins evenly spaced around the rim (every 15 degrees; colours orange, teal, blue, yellow-green, green in no fixed pattern), thin spokes radiating from the red hub, thin concentric circles inside, two red support legs forming an inverted V down from the hub to the ground, small bushes at the base, a street lamp at the left, a ground line. A circled letter E is printed just above the topmost cabin (the orange cabin at 12 o'clock): this marks the starting position. A girl (Reema, orange kurta, long plait) stands at the bottom right outside the wheel looking at it. The picture is used to count turns of the wheel (full turn = back to E, half turn = bottom, quarter turns = 3 o'clock / 9 o'clock positions).

Three round paper fans in a row, each with two ice-cream sticks joined at the fan's centre and a short red arc marking the angle between the two sticks. LEFT fan: one stick pointing straight down, the other pointing down-right (about 30 degrees apart); a small red arc between them at the lower right of the centre (acute). MIDDLE fan: one stick pointing almost straight up (leaning a little right), the other pointing up-left (about 50 to 60 degrees from the first); a red arc across the top-left between them (acute). RIGHT fan: one stick pointing up-left (about 60 degrees left of vertical), the other pointing down and slightly left (about 190 degrees clockwise from vertical); a red arc on the left side between them (about 105 to 110 degrees, obtuse). Fans are green with black radial pleat lines; sticks are yellow; no numbers or labels.

Five circled numbered steps drawn in green paper and yellow ice-cream sticks. Step 1: a wide green rectangle (landscape, about 2:1) with 18 vertical dashed fold lines drawn evenly across it (19 equal strips). Step 2: the paper folded like an accordion/zig-zag: about 10 narrow vertical panels with a zig-zag top and bottom edge (5 raised ridges visible). Step 3: the folded paper seen edge-on as a thin vertical green strip. Step 4: the folded paper pinched at the lower-left end and opened a little into two flared halves (upper and lower fan wings); two yellow ice-cream sticks lie crossed at the left, and two red curved arrows labelled 'Paste' (red italic text) point from the sticks to the fan's two halves (one 'Paste' at the upper left, one 'Paste' at the bottom right). Circle 3: three quarters shaded (everything except the top-left quarter; blue dashed lines from the centre up and from the centre left); pink dashed arrow from the top going clockwise through right and bottom to the left, arrowhead at the left pointing up. Caption: 'This shows a 3/4 turn, which is more than a straight angle.'

Table with a blue rounded outline, 5 columns and 2 rows. Header row (lavender), left to right: 'Full turn' | '1/2 turn (straight angle)' | '1/4 turn (right angle)' | 'Less than a 1/4 turn (acute angle)' | 'Between a 1/4 and 1/2 turn (obtuse angle)' (fractions stacked). (2) 1/2 turn: fan open as a half circle, with both sticks forming one horizontal straight line along the bottom (180 degrees).
